A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ILIAS research. All 24 pages, including supplementary sections A-D, references, tables and qualitative figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval benchmarking, linear-adaptation experiments, reranking comparisons and supplementary analyses, including Tables 2-4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and analyses, with revised mini-ILIAS scores for several models in Table G.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, mini-ILIAS selection, UnED-trained linear adaptation and retrieval/reranking procedures are unchanged in Sections 3-4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: The same ILIAS, mini-ILIAS, UnED and comparison-dataset coverage is retained. Figure 5's change from 'decor' to 'household' corrects a label; household already appears in v2's Figures F and K, with unchanged constituent categories.

E2.justification: The model rosters in Tables 2, G and H are unchanged. Tables 4 and D retain the same alphaQE, CS, SP, AMES, PCAw and Lw comparisons.

E3.justification: Queries, dataset subsets, mAP@1k, train/test resolutions, adaptation budgets and reranking settings remain identical. Table G's numerical revisions are not accompanied by reported protocol changes.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix B retain the same domain, clutter, scale, resolution, adaptation, dimensionality and reranking analyses. Their results and qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain mean and standard deviation over three random distractor subsets in Table 3, and three-seed linear-adaptation robustness reporting in Appendix B.2.

E6.justification: Table G revises 37 of 68 scores in the unadapted 5M mini-ILIAS column, substantially changing comparisons across model families. SigLIP ViT-L at train/test resolutions 384/512 changes from 5.7 to 24.2, DINOv2 ViT-B from 4.6 to 14.3, and USCRR ViT-B from 18.5 to 5.7. These include large ranking reversals under unchanged stated settings. The 100M and adapted columns, and results elsewhere, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The instance-level relevance definition and mathematical descriptions of retrieval and adaptation are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about dataset scale and diversity, linear adaptation, local descriptors and the small image-to-image versus text-to-image performance gap.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving training-domain bias, VLM adaptation, query-expansion failures and clutter/scale sensitivity are identical. Limitations concerning local-descriptor memory and computational costs are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same preprocessing, checkpoints, optimization hyperparameters and resource details. Appendix D's dataset hosting, sharing and licensing information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, all 92 references and the positioning of ILIAS relative to existing datasets and retrieval research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 5's category wording changes from 'decor' to 'household', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The prose and section/appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 corrects one category label while preserving its plotted points and layout. Figures, tables and their placement otherwise remain unchanged; Table G's numerical updates are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reporting consistency. For example, Table G replaces SigLIP-L's 5M score of 5.7 with 24.2, resolving its inconsistency with the unchanged 100M score of 19.6 for the larger distractor set. Figure 5 now agrees with the existing household taxonomy. These are useful repairs, although the main evidence is unchanged and a similar Table G inconsistency remains for ConvNeXt-B trained on in22k (3.2 on 5M versus 6.4 on 100M).
